record.paper_title: Major Unsolved Problems in Space Plasma Physics
record.original_question: In solar-wind magnetohydrodynamic turbulence, why do magnetic-field and velocity-field fluctuation spectra often have a power-law slope close to -5/3, even though the Kolmogorov -5/3 dimensional argument assumes incompressible and isotropic ordinary-fluid turbulence, while the solar wind contains a relatively strong DC magnetic field and Alfvenic turbulence might instead be expected to show a -3/2 slope? Why do density-fluctuation spectra and spectra of fluctuations in the magnetic-field magnitude B also often show -5/3 slopes, and why do some density and magnetic-field-magnitude power spectra flatten at high frequencies while vector magnetic-field and velocity components steepen near the ion-cyclotron dissipation scale?

evidence.quote: Many unsolved issues remain. Why typical spectra of magnetic (or velocity) fluctuations (Matthaeus and Goldstein, 1982) have spectral slopes of ?5/3 is a mystery.
Also puzzling is the fact that spectra of the density fluctuations also have spectral slopes of ?5/3.
the density spectra and the spectra of the fluctuating power in B often show a flattening at high frequencies and that, too, has not been explained.

artifact.status_search_result: The inertial-range spectral index of MHD turbulence (especially the contrast between Kolmogorov $-5/3$ and Iroshnikov–Kraichnan/Boldyrev $-3/2$) remains an actively debated open problem. Recent Parker Solar Probe observations show a radius-dependent index varying between $-5/3$ and $-3/2$, with magnetic and velocity spectra exhibiting different slopes at 1 AU. The behavior of compressive (density and $|\mathbf{B}|$) spectra and their flattening near kinetic scales is still being investigated; no first-principles theory simultaneously accounts for all three observations.

status_evidence.title: Spectral Slope of MHD Turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: A major research effort seeks to unambiguously differentiate between -5/3 and -3/2 power spectral slopes of strong MHD turbulence.
status_evidence.claim: The -5/3 vs -3/2 inertial-range spectral index in MHD turbulence is an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: The Radial Variation of the Solar Wind Turbulence Spectra near the Kinetic Break Scale (Lotz et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral index varies from -5/3 above ~0.4 au toward -3/2 below ~0.2 au.
status_evidence.claim: Observed spectral indices vary with heliocentric distance, complicating a single theoretical explanation.

status_evidence.title: Spectral break of the density power spectrum in solar wind turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2023) study on flattening/break in the density spectrum at kinetic scales.
status_evidence.claim: The behavior of density-fluctuation spectra near the ion scales is still an active research topic.
